reuse.why: All four weekend-handling paths (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and the budget schedule template) go through the shared helpers in shared/schedules.ts instead of re-deriving the rule.

duplication.why: The inline skipWeekend ternaries in schedule-template are removed; only the short 'filter isSkippedWeekendOccurrence then map getDateWithSkippedWeekend' pipeline is repeated in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday rule, the daily-skip rule and holiday parsing all live in shared/schedules.ts next to getNextDate, with server handlers and the budget template only consuming them.

scope.why: Changes stay on the weekend rule, the new handler and holidays; the rename of the schedule data key weekendSolve to weekendSolveMode is a small incidental alignment.

maintainability.why: One WeekendRule type and a handful of named predicates make future rule changes single-point, though the getWeekendSearchWindow heuristic (7 x (1 + holiday count)) and having both a Date and a day-string adjuster with slightly different daily semantics add some cognitive load.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No call site re-implements the weekend rule; all use getDateWithSkippedWeekend/getDayWithSkippedWeekend/isSkippedWeekendOccurrence.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated filter/map pipeline in server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange is visible and short, calling the shared helpers, not a reshaped copy of their logic.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend's solveMode argument became a WeekendRule object that carries holidays and frequency; getDayWithSkippedWeekend has an isDailyWeekendSkip early return; getNextDate keeps its own noSkipWeekend ternary, which is a pre-existing caller option rather than a bypass.
